questions.text: A funeral home embalming room requires mechanical coordination. Which source-safe design approach should be carried into the proposed answer?

options.text: Share the chapel HVAC as a cost-saving default without checking odor, chemical, or health requirements
Provide a separately reviewed exhaust/ventilation strategy and confirm health, sanitation, and mechanical requirements before final sizing
Rely only on natural ventilation because PD 1096 lists a window-opening rule for ordinary rooms
Use one standard commercial HVAC system for all rooms regardless of service function

questions.rationale: The local source packet supports building-code classification and egress, but not a universal numeric HVAC prescription for embalming rooms. The source-safe answer is to require a separately reviewed mechanical strategy and confirm the applicable health/mechanical requirements.
questions.explanation: Shared HVAC allows odor/chemical transmission to chapel; separate system required. Natural ventilation is insufficient for chemical handling and odor control. Standard building HVAC cannot control negative pressure needed for embalming room. Embalming room HVAC must be separate and maintain negative pressure (exhaust > intake) to prevent odor and chemical vapor from migrating to public areas (chapel, viewing room). (Funeral Home Design Standards, HVAC Best Practice) Embalming room requires separate negative-pressure HVAC system for odor/chemical control.
questions.code_citation: Funeral Home Design Standards; HVAC Best Practice

questions.text: For a funeral home, which source-safe regulatory framing should the learner use?

options.text: Only PD 1096 applies, because funeral homes are ordinary commercial buildings
Use PD 1096/RA 9514/BP 344 for building, fire, and accessibility checks, and verify separate health or professional operating rules from the applicable authority
Only the Fire Code applies, because funeral chapels are assembly spaces
Only the local zoning ordinance applies once the use is listed as commercial

questions.rationale: The local packet supports building, fire, accessibility, and funeral-use zoning checks. Operating/licensing claims need their own authority before being stated as exact requirements.

questions.text: A funeral home cold-storage room is being programmed. What should the proposed answer emphasize?

options.text: Use a universal room area from memory without checking the project capacity
Size the room from body capacity, equipment clearances, sanitation workflow, and the applicable health/mechanical requirements
Use the chapel occupant load factor to size cold storage
Place cold storage in public circulation because it is part of the viewing sequence

questions.rationale: No local source in the packet establishes a universal cold-storage area for a specific body count. The source-safe edit removes the exact area endorsement and anchors the answer to program, equipment, sanitation, and mechanical verification.

questions.text: A funeral home cold-storage room requires temperature control. What is the source-safe way to state the requirement?

options.text: No temperature control is needed if the room is near the embalming room
Provide dedicated temperature-controlled storage and verify the exact operating range from the health/mechanical standard or project brief
Use ordinary comfort cooling because the room is inside a commercial occupancy
Use only passive ventilation because PD 1096 includes a window-opening rule

questions.rationale: The local building-code packet supports classification and egress, but not the exact cold-storage temperature range. The proposed answer removes the unsupported exact numeric endorsement.
questions.code_citation: Funeral Home Design Standards; Mortuary Science Practice

questions.text: A funeral home business office adjoins a chapel area. How should the fire-separation answer be framed?

options.text: No separation review is needed if both spaces are under one owner
Verify the required separation from the exact occupancy, hazard, sprinkler, and egress condition under PD 1096/RA 9514
Apply a fixed two-hour wall in all cases without checking the code condition
Use only acoustic separation because the chapel is not a hazardous space

questions.rationale: The local evidence supports mixed-occupancy analysis but not a blanket fire-rating for every funeral-home office/chapel interface. The source-safe answer requires verifying the exact code condition.

questions.text: The minimum area for an embalming room should be determined by:

options.text: A universal NBC minimum area for all funeral homes
The chapel seating capacity only
Functional equipment layout, sanitary workflow, storage, drainage, ventilation, and applicable health/mechanical requirements
The reception-room area divided by the number of viewing rooms

questions.rationale: The local source packet does not establish a universal NBC minimum area for embalming rooms. The source-safe answer removes the unsupported area range and uses functional and regulatory verification.

questions.text: For a funeral home chapel with 300-person seating capacity, how many separate exits are required per the National Building Code?

options.text: 1 exit (sufficient for <100 persons)
2 exits (required at 50+ person occupancy)
3 exits (required for >250 persons)
4 exits (required for all assembly venues)

questions.rationale: Use PD 1096 for occupancy classification and RA 9514/PD 1096 for egress. Treat embalming-room, cold-storage, viewing-room, and HVAC numbers as project-specific health/mechanical/programming requirements unless a local source is cited.

questions.rationale: Use PD 1096 for occupancy classification and RA 9514/PD 1096 for egress. Treat embalming-room, cold-storage, viewing-room, and HVAC numbers as project-specific health/mechanical/programming requirements unless a local source is cited.

questions.text: A funeral home viewing room expects 50 simultaneous visitors. What should a source-audited answer do before giving a final area?

options.text: Use any remembered square-meter-per-visitor rule as if it were code
Ignore furniture and family circulation because only code occupant load matters
Check the applicable occupant-load table and project brief, then size the room for furniture, circulation, and wake practice
Use the chapel exit-width factor as the room-area factor

questions.rationale: The local source packet does not support the old 1.1-1.5 sqm/visitor number as a code rule. The proposed answer removes that exact endorsement and frames the calculation as code plus project-program verification.

questions.text: A funeral home facility contains administrative offices, reception, viewing rooms, a chapel, and embalming/service spaces. How should occupancy classification be structured?

options.text: Classify the entire facility as one assembly occupancy
Classify the entire facility as industrial because cold storage may be present
Use mixed-occupancy analysis: business/mercantile areas under Group E, chapel areas under the applicable assembly group, and service spaces checked by their hazard/use
Classify the facility only by the largest room

questions.rationale: PD 1096 supports occupancy classification by use/character and includes Group E business/mercantile and assembly group provisions. Funeral uses also appear in local zoning/use tables. Mixed-occupancy analysis is the source-safe answer.
